cvEn:
Shimon Meir, son of Miriam and Meir, was born in 1947 (5707) in India and immigrated to Israel with his family in 1954. The family settled in Almah, a moshav in the Galilee, where they earned their livelihood from farming. Shimon spent his elementary school years in this community. When he reached the age of Bar Mitzvah, the family moved to Avi'ezer, a moshav in the Adullam region of the Valley of Elah. He studied at the 'Even HaEzer' regional high school in the moshav of Nahom. He was an active, hard-working young man in the youth society, showing initiative and readiness to help others when needed. For this he was loved and well regarded in the moshav.

Shimon was drafted into compulsory service in the IDF in November 1964 and was assigned to the Supply Corps. After his release from compulsory service he returned to the moshav and continued to lead an agricultural lifestyle. In 1974 he married Sarah, and the couple had four children: Shmuel, Merit, Tamnat and Avi. Shimon was a loving father and a devoted family man. In January 1988 he was called up for reserve service in the Air Force. He fell during his service on 1 Shevat 5748 (19 January 1988) and was laid to rest in the military cemetery on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem. He left behind his wife, four children, his father, six brothers – Nehemiah, Menahem, Avraham, Eliezer, Rachamim and Reuven – and four sisters – Miriam, Leah, Rachel and Adina. The family commemorated his memory with a synagogue.
